summary.headline: Amber FY26 consolidated revenue rose 22% to INR12,186 crore, but management flags 50-100 bps consolidated margin pressure in FY27 from commodity and wage costs.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue grew 22% to INR12,186 crore and operating EBITDA grew 22% to INR970 crore, with adjusted PAT of INR338 crore (up 22%). Q4 revenue rose 10% to INR4,148 crore, operating EBITDA rose 15% to INR362 crore, and adjusted PAT rose 27% to INR162 crore. Management guided to a temporary 50-100 bps consolidated margin squeeze in FY27 from copper clad laminate and gold costs, currency depreciation and minimum wage hikes. Electronics is guided to about 40% growth in FY27 at 9.5-10% margin after a job-work conversion, and Railways to 30-35% growth at 16-17% margin.

segments.name: Consumer Durables
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR8,383 crore (+14%) against a flat RAC industry; EBITDA INR593 crore (+6%). Management guides FY27 growth in line with the industry at about 12-13%, with percentage margin diluted by price hikes but per-unit margin intact. Non-RAC is about 32% of consolidated revenue.

segments.name: Electronics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR3,268 crore (+49%) and EBITDA INR287 crore (+89%), about 8.8% margin. PCBA is about INR2,281 crore at roughly 5% margin; PCB is about INR600 crore at 12-13% margin. FY27 guided to about 40% growth at 9.5-10% margin after two customers moved from purchase to job-work agreements.

segments.name: Railway Systems and Defense
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR535 crore (+19%) and EBITDA INR90 crore (+8%). Order book above INR2,600 crore. Sidwal's Faridabad greenfield plant is in trial production with commercial production expected this quarter; FY27 and FY28 growth guided at 30-35% with 16-17% margin.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated margin pressure of 50-100 bps in FY27, described as temporary and expected to normalise as the macro environment improves.
Consumer Durables FY27 growth to track the RAC industry at about 12-13%, after industry growth of about 20% in Q1 FY27.
Electronics FY27 revenue growth of about 40% with 9.5-10% EBITDA margin.
Railways FY27 and FY28 growth of 30-35%, margin 16-17%, subject to no disruption in Indian Railways or Metro offtake.
FY27 gross capex of INR1,800-2,000 crore, of which cash outflow is about INR1,100-1,200 crore after supplier credit terms; FY28 cash outflow about INR1,400-1,500 crore.
Net debt expected to rise to INR700-800 crore by March 2027. PLI receipts: INR49.5 crore received in April 2026 for FY25 and INR78 crore expected for FY26.
capex_capacity: Ascent-K Circuit HDI PCB plant in Noida: construction to start around June 2026, 15-16 months to build, then 3-4 months of trial production; mass production from Q3-Q4 FY28. Backed by over INR4,500 crore of ECMS investment approvals across Ascent-K, Ascent and Shogini.
Ascent Circuits Hosur: construction delayed about one quarter by a pollution consent issue; trial production by Q3 FY27 and commercial production by mid-February 2027.

FY26 total capex about INR1,070 crore, of which INR550 crore capitalised and the balance in CWIP for operations in FY27. FY27 capex of about INR1,200 crore for Ascent plus INR700-800 crore for other entities.

Subsidies: about 48% of plant and machinery via ECMS and 42% from the UP government on building and plant and machinery, received with a 5-6 year lag. Land received at about a 25% discount; the subsidy flow is expected from FY28.

Sri City RAC capacity augmented. Railway Faridabad greenfield plant in trial production. Yujin factory in Korea completed, awaiting RDSO approval (12-15 months), with INR178 crore couplers order book.
demand_pricing: Industry view: RAC volumes were down about 30% in Q1 and Q2 FY26 and recovered in Q3-Q4, leaving FY26 roughly flat. Industry expected to grow about 20% in Q1 FY27 and 12-13% for FY27.

Price increases of about 14% YoY on finished goods: one in January 2026 from the star-rating change and one in April 2026 for commodity costs. Copper clad laminate prices are up more than 60% in one year and still rising; gold is up about 60%.
PCB pricing: Tier 1 EMS pass-through works on a quarterly lag, but PCB (Tier 2) has about a two-quarter lag. Two price increases of about 15% and 18% have been received, with more under negotiation.
Compressor import relief: government allowed imports of about 30% of last year's volumes for compressors below 2 tonne, extended for a year. Management says there is no compressor shortage.
Electronics margin pressure: PCBA about 5% and PCB about 12-13% versus a normal 16-17%. Management expects the price increases to flow through over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the RAC industry growth expectations for Q1 and FY27, and which segments face margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry expected to grow about 20% in Q1 FY27 and 12-13% for the full year. Margin pressure comes from minimum wage hikes (35% in Haryana, about 22% in UP), CCL and gold costs, and currency depreciation. Indian Railway fixed-price contracts cannot pass costs through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10-12% price increase reasonable?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases are about 14% YoY, from a January star-rating change and an April commodity-driven hike.

qa_highlights.question: Will compressor shortages hurt FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says there is no shortage. Five new domestic manufacturers have come up, and imports of 30% of last year's volumes are allowed. Commercial AC compressors are still largely imported.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Consumer Durables finished-goods share rise, and is it realisation-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished goods rose because gas-charging customers moved to ODM solutions, not because of realisation. Finished goods fell from about 80% at listing in FY18 to about 40% now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PCB versus PCBA mix and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 Electronics: PCBA about INR2,281 crore at about 5% margin; PCB about INR600 crore at 12-13%; Power-One about 15% margin; Unitronics not disclosed as it is listed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and net cash outflow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 gross capex INR1,800-2,000 crore with cash outflow of about INR1,100-1,200 crore. FY28 cash outflow of about INR1,400-1,500 crore.

risks_watch: FY27 margin squeeze of 50-100 bps from commodity inflation, currency depreciation and minimum wage revisions in UP, Haryana and other states.
PCB price pass-through lag of about two quarters and the Tier 2 position, which limit near-term recovery.
Net debt rising to INR700-800 crore by March 2027 while capex is heavy; working capital days up to 29 from 9 due to inventory build.
Ascent Hosur construction delay (about one quarter) and Ascent-K HDI timelines; subsidies arrive with a 5-6 year lag.
Non-controlling interest from CCPS: auditors assumed about 30% dilution as a maximum, with actual dilution expected to be lower; NCI remains a balance-sheet item.
Electronics customer shifts from purchase to job-work could cause organic top-line volatility; organic growth was subdued in Q4.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and capacity, with an explicit caution on near-term margins. Management was candid about the 50-100 bps FY27 squeeze and the PCB lag, and gave specific numbers for capex and cash flow. Management declined to give Unitronics-level detail because it is listed.
key_quotes: So our endeavor on going towards the value side of the businesses is because in B2B business, what we are trying to attempt is we are trying to balance the left and right.
To sum up, we expect a margin pressure of 50 to 100 bps at consolidated level, which is of temporary in nature and expected to normalize as macro environment improves.
